patients.label: Female newborn with a prenatally detected pelvic cystic mass, treated by hymenectomy on the second day after vaginal delivery

identity_evidence.quote: she gave birth to a 3200-g female alive newborn

attribution_limitations: The index patient is the fetus and newborn. Maternal facts (age, gravidity, labor induction, counseling, referral) carry the subject label mother, antenatal findings the label fetus, and postnatal facts the label index_patient.

The abstract says the case was diagnosed with congenital hydrometrocolpos at 39 weeks of gestation and that huge hydrometrocolpos secondary to imperforate hymen was diagnosed postnatally; the discussion says prenatal ultrasound diagnosed the hydrometrocolpos and its cause (imperforate hymen) was confirmed after delivery. This is read as antenatal detection with postnatal confirmation of the cause, an ambiguity in wording, not a source conflict.
The woman was told at the obstetric ultrasound that her fetus was in good condition; this reported statement is not recorded as an observation.

The case text describes a routine ultrasound for a biophysical profile that saw the fetal mass and a later referral for advanced ultrasound at 39 weeks of gestation, while the abstract places the diagnosis at 39 weeks during routine third-trimester scanning. Whether the routine scan and the 39-week advanced scan are separate examinations, and their order, is not stated.
